cases.description: Fictional sample data for application testing. A complaint alleges that a two-wheeler motorcycle was removed without permission from a public parking area. The investigating team should record the complainant statement and vehicle registration, make, model, colour, and chassis details; examine available CCTV; identify witnesses; verify the parking location; and check vehicle movement records where legally authorized. Preserve all evidence with timestamps and chain of custody. Investigation remains ongoing pending verification, identification of a suspect, and recovery of the vehicle. Applicable law and priority require verification by the investigating authority.

FICTIONAL INVESTIGATION REPORT — NOT AN OFFICIAL RECORD  Application testing / demonstration only   Page 1  INVESTIGATION REPORT  Alleged Theft of a Two-Wheeler Motorcycle  FICTIONAL SAMPLE FOR APPLICATION TESTING — NOT AN OFFICIAL POLICE REPORT  All names, addresses, contact details, vehicle identifiers, dates, timestamps, and investigative events in this report are invented for demonstration. At around 10:00 PM, he returned and found the vehicle missing. He states that he made brief enquiries nearby but could not locate it, and suspects an unidentified person may have removed it without permission. These statements are invented and remain allegations within the sample scenario.  3. It is an AI-generated illustration, not a frame extracted from an actual camera system. Its scene, depicted individual, vehicle, and displayed timestamp are fabricated. Assessment and Limitations  The information currently represented in this sample is insufficient to reach a factual conclusion about the occurrence of an offence, the identity of any offender, or the whereabouts of the motorcycle. Conclusion  For this fictional scenario, the case remains open and unverified. No suspect has been identified, no vehicle has been recovered, and no authentic evidence has been examined. FICTIONAL FORENSIC SAMPLE — NOT AN ACCREDITED LABORATORY REPORT   1  DIGITAL FORENSIC EXAMINATION REPORT  SIMULATED TRAINING REPORT — NOT AN OFFICIAL FORENSIC FINDING  Case CASE-2026-0045 | Alleged theft of two-wheeler motorcycle | Report date: 22 October 2026. All persons, vehicle details, investigative events, and findings are fictional. The attached image was AI-generated and is not CCTV evidence.  1. Case Identification  Case docket   CASE-2026-0045 Incident   Alleged motorcycle theft from a public parking area Jurisdiction   Central Jurisdiction Local Police Station (fictional) Crime reference   Motor vehicle theft; BNS Section 303(2) subject to verification Sample complainant   Arun Kumar (fictional) Illustrative vehicle   Black Honda Activa 6G, sample registration TN 00 AB 1234 Examiner   Demo Digital Forensics Analyst (fictional role) Document classification   Educational application-testing specimen; not a certified report  2. Scope and Material Examined  This exercise examines only the previously generated CCTV-style illustration as a digital file. No original camera recording, DVR/NVR device, witness material, vehicle, or scene evidence was received. No physical forensic examination, image authentication, biometric identification, or video continuity analysis was performed.  Mock exhibit ID   CCTV-02 Source   AI-generated image created for application testing File type   PNG image File size   2,274,192 bytes Image dimensions   1672 x 941 pixels SHA-256 of this PNG   818c804806b457231339c4d553a1196f 7939ad192ffd11dcfb7838655b01626f Hash interpretation   Computed for this illustrative file only; not proof of CCTV provenance  3. Methodology  The demonstration workflow consisted of (a) recording the file identity, format, dimensions, and byte length; (b) calculating a SHA-256 digest of the supplied PNG; (c) visually inspecting the illustration; and (d) documenting limitations and preservation recommendations. The digest identifies these exact file bytes; it does not verify the depicted events or the claimed capture time.  4. Observations and Interpretation

FICTIONAL FORENSIC SAMPLE — NOT AN ACCREDITED LABORATORY REPORT   2  Visible scene:   The illustrative frame depicts a public parking area, motorcycles, and a highlighted person near a motorcycle.  Overlay information:   Camera and timestamp overlays are part of the generated illustration, not verified camera metadata.  Authenticity:   The image is known to be AI-generated. It is unsuitable for establishing that a real theft took place.  Suspect identification:   No real suspect identification can be made from this illustration.  Vehicle identification:   No real vehicle ownership, registration, or chassis details were authenticated.  Time reconstruction:   The illustrated timestamp is not evidence of when any real-world event occurred.  5. Chain of Custody and Evidentiary Status  CCTV-02 is a mock exhibit. Its origin in the application demonstration is known, but it has no genuine surveillance-device acquisition record, source-system log, or lawful seizure documentation. A real chain-of-custody record would require the collector, acquisition time and time zone, device/source, export method, storage location, integrity hash, and every handover. No such real evidentiary chain is asserted here.

FICTIONAL FORENSIC SAMPLE — NOT AN ACCREDITED LABORATORY REPORT   3  6. Findings  F-01: The supplied PNG is an AI-generated illustration, not a verified CCTV export. F-02: The SHA-256 digest above can be used to check whether this specific sample file changes. F-03: The illustration cannot support a forensic conclusion concerning an actual offence, suspect, vehicle, or timeline. F-04: No genuine CCTV footage or physical exhibits were available for examination.  7. Recommendations for an Actual Examination  • Obtain the original recording from the relevant DVR/NVR or camera system through authorized procedures. • Record camera location, system clock accuracy, export process, and collection timestamps. • Retain the original media read-only and compute cryptographic hashes on acquisition and transfer. • Review relevant footage in temporal context and separately document any enhancements or annotations. • Correlate video observations with verified registration records, scene observations, and witness statements. • Have a qualified examiner document methods, tools, limitations, and independently reviewable results.  8. Conclusion  No forensic determination about the alleged theft can be reached from the available material. The only demonstrable technical result is the computed SHA-256 digest of the mock image file. The fictional investigation remains unverified, with no authenticated CCTV evidence, suspect identification, or vehicle recovery established.  9.
